To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

macrophages use a TLR-independent pathway that is mediated by the cytosolic receptor NOD2 to detect bacterial degradation products that are generated inside a phago-lysosomal compartment and transported to the macrophage cytosol.
macrophages can detect bacterial ligands generated during the degradation of bacteria in the phagosomes and that the innate immune receptors that detect these ligands are cytosolic.
the activation of cytosolic receptors by bacterial ligands released into the cytosol is a critical step in the activation of macrophage responses against intracellular bacteria.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how macrophages sense and respond to intracellular pathogens and how the innate immune system can be activated to promote protective immunity.
understanding the cellular mechanisms by which macrophages recognize and respond to intracellular bacteria.
understanding the mechanisms of host cell recognition and response to bacterial infection, and the molecular and cellular basis for the innate and cell-mediated immune response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the innate immune system of activated macrophages monitors the fate of internalised bacteria and responds specifically to bacterial ligands that are generated in the phago lysosome.
NOD2, a cytosolic sensor of peptidoglican, detects bacterial ligands generated by lysosomal proteases during the degradation of intracellular bacteria in phagosomes.
the phagosome is a dynamic compartment that is capable of generating ligands that are recognized by cytosolic sensors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

macrophages can sense bacteria that are degraded in the phagolysosome, and that this response is mediated by cytosolic innate receptors that recognize bacterial ligands generated during phagosome maturation.
the cytosolic innate immunity system is activated by bacterial ligand generation and transport to the cytosolic compartment.
macrophages are able to sense the fate of intracellular pathogens and that the fate of a pathogen is sensed by cytosolic receptors that are not normally activated in resting macrophages.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fate of bacteria in macrophages is monitored by the activation of a specific gene expression profile.
bacterial ligands generated by degradation of intracellular bacteria in the phagolysosome are targets of the cytosolic innate immunity system.
the cytosolic innate immunity system is able to monitor the fate of intracellular bacteria and to induce a specific transcriptional response to bacteria degraded in the phagolysosome.
